text:
mia: FYI saw a weird spike in eval-runner queue this morning, looks like some shards got 'stuck' and starved other jobs. throughput dropped ~40% for quant evals

jordan: ugh. which job? any logs or trace id?

mia: shard-affinity job for the new 4-bit quantization tests (q4f). root log snippet: 
```
2026-03-11T08:14:23Z worker-12 INFO lease acquired shard=23 job=eval-q4f-20260311
2026-03-11T08:14:23Z worker-12 INFO start batch size=64
2026-03-11T08:14:40Z worker-12 WARN blocked on kv-cache wait 17s
2026-03-11T08:15:10Z worker-12 ERROR lease renewal failed: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-11T08:15:10Z worker-12 INFO shard=23 orphaned
```
looks like a lease renewal race + heavy kv-cache stall. lots of retries queued behind that shard.

sanjay: does this correlate with the new shard-affinity scheduling change we rolled last week? that change pins shards to the same worker to improve KV locality, but might amplify head-of-line blocking.

mia: yes that's my hunch. before affinity we had more implicit load-balancing across workers so stalls were spread out. with affinity a single slow shard can create backpressure for all its pending buckets.

jordan: can we repro locally with the stress harness? lucy, you added the affinity tests last sprint, any ideas on reproducer?

lucy: i hit this in staging. quick reproducer: spawn N=8 workers, pin shard 23 to worker-12, then inject a 20s artificial stall on kv-cache lookup for requests with prefix "quant-debug". i can paste the patch i used.

```
--- a/runner/kv_cache.go
+++ b/runner/kv_cache.go
@@ -12,6 +12,10 @@ func GetKV(prefix string) {
+ if strings.HasPrefix(prefix, "quant-debug") {
+   time.Sleep(20 * time.Second) // simulate slow network
+ }
```

this reliably blocks the worker and you see the queue depth on the other workers climb.

mia: metrics we saw: per-shard lease-ttl drop to 0, worker cpu idle low, request_wait_seconds histogram shifts right. triggering our backpressure alarm: `eval.queue.depth > 200`

jordan: ok. short-term mitigation? maybe add lease preemption/steal when renewals fail or bounded affinity expiry? and patch the kv-cache to early-fail on long tail lookups.

sanjay: agree. two-pronged: (1) make affinity soft by adding an affinity_ttl so shards can be rebalanced after X seconds of inactivity or when renewals fail; (2) add a per-request kv timeout plus fast-fail hook that marks the lease as errored so other waiting requests can be routed elsewhere.

lucy: i can do (2) and add a small integration test in eval-ci that injects a kv stall and asserts that pipeline continues with <10% throughput loss. will need a small change in the harness to surface the fast-fail metric `kv.request.fast_fail` so we can assert.

mia: also worth adding a dashboard panel for shard-affinity hit rate and lease_renewal_failures per worker. right now we only have job-level metrics, hard to correlate.

jordan: good call. add a per-worker heatmap and a new alert: `sum(lease_renewal_failures) by (worker) > 5 for 5m`

sanjay: caution: make sure the steal policy doesn't thrash. affinity_ttl should be conservative, e.g. 90s, and use exponential backoff for steals. we don't want to bounce shards during transient hiccups.

lucy: patch plan: open PR with kv timeout + metric (small change), add unit & integration test in eval-harness, add playground deploy to staging. follow-up PR to runtime to add affinity_ttl + steal logic (needs more review).

mia: timeline? this is impacting nightly quant regression runs, so target is hotfix for staging in next 48h, and full rollout in one week if metrics are green.

jordan: assign tasks: lucy -> kv timeout + tests, sanjay -> affinity_ttl design + proto, mia -> dashboard + alert, i'll coordinate CI gating and do the staging deploy.

eval-bot: alert: eval.queue.depth breached (2026-03-11T08:17:00Z) - incident created id=EVAL-9483 :bell:

lucy: starting PR now, will tag @jordan for review. expecting small risk. :thumbsup:

sanjay: i'll draft the affinity_ttl RFC today, ping when ready for review.

jordan: nice work catching this — probably would've been worse once larger shard sets come online. good to have the backpressure/metrics added to catch early.

mia: thanks team. i'll post an update in #eng-oncall after staging deploy.

lucy: FYI the integration test asserts the harness continues processing other shards within 20s and that we emit `kv.request.fast_fail=1` at least once.

jordan: perfect. after hotfix we should run a full quant benchmark and compare token/s and quality metrics to ensure the fix doesn't alter scheduling in a way that impacts latency SLOs.

mia: agree — add the benchmark run to the PR checklist. closing the loop once staging green. :white_check_mark:
